title: VS Code 1.141 Brings Copilot, Codex Sessions Together, Tightens AI Agent Security
source_used: Visual Studio Code 1.141 release notes (code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_141); Visual Studio Magazine blocked (HTTP 403)
key_facts: Visual Studio Code 1.141 is marked "Released October 7, 2026" on the stable channel.

The release notes list: cleaning up worktree storage of inactive agent sessions, cross-platform terminal sandboxing, arranging sessions in a grid, continuing external Copilot and Codex sessions, block pasting, and multiple GitHub Enterprise instances.
Terminal sandboxing limits agent access to files and network resources on Windows, macOS and Linux.

Microsoft says sandboxing helps reduce the impact of model mistakes, prompt injection, untrusted dependencies and locally launched tool servers, but does not replace endpoint security or provide a standalone security boundary.
A Codex chat started in the ChatGPT app or Codex CLI can be continued in the Agents window with its history intact; only one application can send messages to the chat at a time.
quote_evidence: This release makes it easier to manage agent sessions, protect agent workflows, edit columnar text, and work across GitHub Enterprise instances.
Cross-platform sandboxing: Limit agent access to files and network resources on Windows, macOS, and Linux with terminal sandboxing.
Sandboxing adds a layer of protection, but does not replace endpoint security or provide a standalone security boundary.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers who let AI agents run commands get a built-in way to restrict what the agents can touch.
notes: The pool item (Visual Studio Magazine, 13 Oct 2026) was blocked with HTTP 403, so I wrote from Microsoft's official release notes, which show the release came out on 7 Oct 2026, six days before the coverage. Stale, so score lowered and freshness marked FOLLOW-UP.
